newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Syrian vice-president meets Moroccan king.
newsitem.headline: Syrian vice-president meets Moroccan king.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam, on a tour of North African countries to build support for Syria's stand in Middle East peace, met Moroccan King Hassan late on Monday.

The official Moroccan news agency MAP said Khaddam and Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara held talks with the king at a meeting also attended by Moroccan Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, but gave no further details.
Khaddam arrived in Morocco on Monday and called on the United States to put pressure on Israel to resume talks with Damascus.
"Syria is ready for the talks with Israel on the condition that the negotiations begin from the point where they broke (last year)," Khaddam told reporters shortly after his arrival at Rabat airport.
"Syria expects his majesty King Hassan's support for Syria's stand in the Middle East peace process," Shara said.
Khaddam reiterated that Damascus would resume negotiations with the Jewish state only after Israel agreed to return the Golan Heights, which it captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

Asked about a U.S. role in possible Israeli-Syrian negotiations, Khaddam said: "We are ready for the negotiations but it is up to the United States to convince Israel to respect its previous commitments."
Israel broke off talks after a wave of Islamist bombings in Israel last February and March.
A resumption of talks is stymied by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to negotiate the return of land.
